Recent market reports showed BTC briefly crossing the $80,000 mark, supported by renewed institutional demand and large spot bitcoin ETF inflows. Ether has also been part of the same liquidity story, with ETH demand helping broaden risk appetite into major altcoins. Stablecoins remain one of the strongest structural stories. U.S. policy debate increasingly connects regulated dollar tokens with payments, Treasury-bill demand and global dollar access. If the 5-day moving average is above, only go long; if it’s below, only go short. Don’t fight the trend—you’ll die a miserable death.

3. Cut fast when you’re wrong
Once a key level breaks, cut immediately. Don’t fall in love with the position. If the market comes back after you cut, then re-enter—better than getting liquidated.

4. Adding to the position is the real way
After catching the first wave, wait for a pullback to support and add again. Remember: adding must be as cautious as your very first entry.

5. Use a trailing stop
Every time you add, move your stop-loss up. In the end, only profit is left to run—you can sleep soundly.

6. Let the profits fly
Don’t act like you’ve never seen money—if you gain 10%, don’t just run. The real “fat meat” is later. Wait for clear top signals, then dump all at once.

If you have less than 2,000 U in your hands, don’t try to copy the big-name V’s. The tricks used by institutions often make people trading crypto get more and more complicated, yet they earn less and less.

As for me—from 30,000 to 10 million. It wasn’t insider information, and it wasn’t talent. It was simplicity and going to the extreme.

First phase: 30k → 1.2m, took 2 years.
Second phase: 1.2m → 6m, took 1 year.
Final phase: 6m → 10m, took 5 months.

The further I went, the more I realized a rule: the speed of making money is inversely proportional to the number of times you “take action.” The simpler and more focused you are, the more you can earn.

I focus on only one pattern—"the N shape".
A vertical surge upward, then a diagonal pullback, and then another vertical breakout.
When the N shape forms, I enter. When the N shape breaks down, I cut my position.
No adding to the position, no increasing leverage, and no holding through the pain.
Set stop-loss at 2%, take-profit at 10%. With a win rate of 35%, you can keep making profits.

Many people think this approach is too “stupid” and like to watch indicators, draw trend lines, and check news—resulting in losses that happen even faster.

But I do the opposite and keep it simple:
Only keep the 20-day moving average, fade its color to reduce distractions.
Every morning at 9:50, open the exchange and scan the 4-hour chart—
No N shape? Shut it down.
If there is an N shape? Place the order, with stop-loss and take-profit.
I spend only 5 minutes all day; the rest of the time I drink coffee and walk my dog.
When I make money, I follow three steps:
When I reach 1.2m, I first withdraw the principal;
When I reach 6m, I take half to buy funds and put the money into fixed deposits;
The rest keeps rolling.
Even if the market collapses, the foundation is still solid.
There is no holy grail in the crypto world—only sieves.
If you sieve long enough, the gold will naturally remain.

Don’t always think about 100x coins. If you can consistently take 10% for 20 trades, you’ll realize—10 million is really just a matter of time.
I’ve walked through the night; the torch has already been handed to you. Will you follow it 👉@Square-Creator-58b326784 #龙虾 #ETH

My take: short/ bearish direction feels more comfortable. If it spikes toward 0.55 but volume still can’t keep up, you could consider a light short position. Stop-loss: above 0.58. Target: 0.49. Rough risk-reward is about 1:1.7—just so-so. But honestly, MAGMA swings too much. You must control position size. If it breaks above 0.58 with expanded volume, the bearish thesis is directly invalid—don’t stubbornly hold.

DEXE: 2.4250. This one is kind of interesting. It’s third in the gainers list at +27.5%, but its volume is steady at 1.0x average volume—healthier than the first two. My view: among these three, it might be the most worth watching. Short-term idea: pull back to around 2.344 for a bullish entry. Stop-loss: below 2.25. Target: 2.705. Risk-reward is roughly 1:2.2. If it breaks above 2.705 with volume, you can look for higher.

Invalidation conditions: it drops below 2.344 and volume increases—this would suggest the move is basically a bull-trap.

Overall: today’s top three gainers share a common trait—while the broader market is down, they’re pulling against the trend. But this kind of counter-trend move often has questionable follow-through. Fear & Greed at 35 means sentiment is cautious. In this situation, chasing the highs isn’t very cost-effective. My stance is very clear: wait for the pullback—don’t rush.

Some people might say, “You’re too conservative. It’s pumping so hard—you’re missing out by not chasing.” But I’ve seen too many people die chasing highs (manual doge head). A low-volume rally itself is a warning signal—especially when the broader market mood is weak. If you genuinely think it’s good, it’s never too late to enter after it pulls back and confirms support. You might make a bit less, but your safety margin is way higher.

On the flip side, look at the decliners list: HUMA -25%, CYS -23%, TAC -19%. These are coins that may have pumped earlier the past few days, and today they’re collectively pulling back. Market rotation is happening too fast. Today’s star can easily become tomorrow’s sacrificial lamb. In this kind of rhythm, controlling position size matters more than anything.

In the futures contract market, there are too many people going long, and leverage is stacked. When it’s like this, the biggest risk is that the main players flip the other way and shake the market (liquidation sweep). I suffered a similar loss last week—I chased a coin whose funding rate suddenly spiked, and then got slapped by a single big bearish candle (too much talk and it’s just tears). So at this lobster position, short-term I don’t recommend blindly chasing higher. If you want to get involved, a long-biased reference zone is around 0.0577–0.0620 while waiting for a pullback. Put the stop loss below 0.0540. First target: 0.069. Let’s calculate the risk-reward: entry 0.06, stop 0.054, target 0.069. RR is about 1:1.5. Honestly, that payout is just average. Also pay attention: it’s a price increase on decreasing volume—0.4x average volume. What does that mean? A volume-shrinking pump is a warning sign; it suggests the chasing funds aren’t fully committed. If later it breaks above 0.069 with increased volume and holds, then that’s the real acceleration signal—no rush to join until then.

Next MAGMA: +32.67% to 0.5195. Volume is steady at 0.7x average volume. The current price is at about 80% of the range; 24h high is 0.5796 and support is 0.491. 【ETH has been stuck sideways at $ 2440 for almost a week—what are the pros watching?】

Recently, Ripple said they are preparing a quantum-resistant plan for XRP. Bitcoin and Ethereum have also issued migration plans. Crypto media is in an uproar, with everyone shouting, "The quantum threat is here."

But I think this actually indicates one thing: the major chains are taking this issue seriously. If they’re taking it seriously, it means it’s not yet that urgent. Still, the signal itself is worth pondering—who is really doing the work, and who’s just riding the hype. People in the industry all know the answer.

Back to ETH. At the level $ 2440, ETH is down 2.2% over 24 hours and down 3% over 7 days—basically just going sideways. Trading volume has been fairly active, suggesting everyone is watching, but nobody dares to make the first move.

My view: over the next 7 days, ➡️ expect range-bound trading.

There are three reasons.

First, the technicals haven’t given a clear direction yet. There have been consecutive small declines, but the key support hasn’t been broken. This kind of movement most commonly turns into continued grinding.

Second, the Fear & Greed Index is 68, slightly lower than last week’s 70. Sentiment is cooling, but it hasn’t reached extreme panic. That actually suggests the market is still relatively rational.

Third, BTC’s dominance has climbed to 59%. Capital is flowing toward BTC. This isn’t great news for ETH, but it’s also not a fatal problem—if BTC stabilizes, ETH will have room to move.

Honestly, ETH has pulled back more than 50% from its highs. At this point, long-term funds have already started looking. I’m not saying it will rise immediately, but in this range, value investors will enter in batches.

Where could my call be wrong? If this week directly breaks below $ 2200, then I’ll accept it. If suddenly there’s a volume expansion and it pushes above $ 2700, I’ll accept that too. Right now, there’s no reason to heavily bet on a directional move.

So I care more about one question: when this becomes real, what does it mean in practice?

The project teams are preparing, institutions are observing, and retail investors are waiting for signals. The ones truly affected are the projects that haven’t upgraded to quantum-resistant plans yet—they’re the most vulnerable in this wave. From a business logic standpoint, whoever completes the migration first can win trust and endorsements in the next round of competition. This isn’t a technical issue—it’s a matter of time.

What about you—do you think this round of ETH will keep grinding sideways, or is it building up for a big move? Come back next week and compare.

【ETH在$ 2440横了快一周，老手都在盯着什么】

最近Ripple说他们在给XRP准备抗量子方案，比特币和以太坊也发了迁移计划。币圈媒体炸了锅，都在喊"量子威胁来了"。

我倒觉得这恰恰说明一件事：主流链都在认真对待这个问题。认真对待，就意味着还没那么紧迫。但这个信号本身值得琢磨——谁在真干、谁在蹭热点，圈内人都门清。

回到ETH。$ 2440这个位置，24小时跌了2.2%，7天跌了3%，说白了就是横着。成交量倒是挺活跃，说明大家都在看着，但没人敢先动手。

我的判断：未来7天，➡️震荡。

理由有三。

第一，技术面还没给出方向。连续小跌，但没破关键支撑，这种走势最常见的就是继续磨。第二，恐惧贪婪指数68，比上周70还低了一点，情绪在降温，但没到恐慌那种极端，反而说明市场还理性。第三，BTC的占比冲到59%了，资金在往BTC聚，这不是ETH的利好，但也不算什么致命问题——BTC稳了，ETH才有空间。

说真的，ETH从高点回撤了50%多，这个位置长线资金已经开始看了。我不是说马上涨，但这个区间，价值投资者会分批进场。

什么情况我判断错了？如果这周直接跌破$ 2200，那我认；如果突然放量冲过$ 2700，那我也认。现在这个位置，没道理重仓赌方向。

所以我更关心一件事：这件事落到实处意味着什么？

项目方在做准备，机构在观望，散户在等信号。真正受影响的是那些还没升级抗量子方案的小项目——他们才是这波里最脆弱的。商业逻辑上看，谁先搞定迁移，谁就能在下一轮竞争里抢到信任背书。这不是技术问题，是时间问题。

你呢，你觉得这波ETH是继续磨，还是憋个大的？下周回来对照。

Three Coins to Benefit from Grayscale’s “Debt Inflation” Narrative: Beyond BTC and ETH, There’s One Overlooked Pick

Grayscale research believes runaway U.S. Treasury debt is positive for BTC, ETH, and ZEC—this is the new narrative of a “currency devaluation trade.”

In its report, Grayscale said that U.S. government debt continues to balloon with no sign of control. Over the long run, it will erode people’s confidence in fiat currency, and capital will look for alternative stores of value. It specifically named three beneficiaries: Bitcoin, Ethereum, and the more niche Zcash. The logic is straightforward: the higher the debt piled up → weaker expected purchasing power of the dollar → a premium for scarce assets. BTC is currently at $78,018, ETH at $2,450.75—basically unchanged—suggesting the market has not yet priced in this narrative.

Impact on the market
- Short term: This is narrative-level bullishness, not liquidity-level bullishness. Don’t expect a major surge within 12 hours. Still, Grayscale is an institution managing large money, and such reports may gradually seep into discussions about institutional positioning.
- Medium term: Debt monetization is the macro main theme of the coming years. Once rate cuts and deficit expansion resonate together, this logic will be repeatedly traded. ZEC being singled out is a small surprise; historically, when Grayscale named smaller coins, those coins often saw short-term bursts of inflows.

My take
I agree with this direction. Long term, the bullish logic holds. But in terms of timing, this is a slow-moving variable. With BTC ranging around $78,018, price action driven by narrative usually first shows up in the ETH/BTC ratio and in small-cap coins like ZEC, while BTC itself tends to wait for macro data confirmation. Key risk: if fiscal tightening comes in stronger than expected or the U.S. dollar strengthens, this narrative could temporarily fizzle out. The focus should be on subsequent data on the U.S. Treasury’s bond issuance size—that’s the hard indicator for validating this logic.

Aug 30: BTC Recent Market Conditions, and Next Week’s Outlook

In the recent livestream room, the orders everyone placed were all in the thousands and above. Within a week, all my friends managed to complete trades both big and small. This week, Bitcoin (“big pie”) has gone through a full round of the “policy roller-coaster.” On August 25, it briefly touched above $81,000—first time returning to the $80k level since mid-May. However, by August 28, the price rapidly fell from the intraday high around $81,330 back to around the $77,300 area.

The most clear macro catalyst for this round of pullback was Fed Chair Powell’s remarks at the Jackson Hole Global Central Banking conference. He said inflation has not shown a “meaningful and sustained slowdown,” that the 2% inflation target is “firm and unshakable,” and even claimed that the forward guidance introduced during the financial crisis is “outdated.”

From a technical perspective, after BTC topped at $81,330 on the daily chart, it formed a “bearish engulfing” pattern—one large bearish candle fully covering the previous day’s bullish candle. RSI has fallen from the extremely overbought level of 85 to about 71. Combined with the 4-hour Bollinger Bands, $77,900 is still stuck between the lower band at $76,805 and the midline at $78,703. In other words, the bears hold initiative on the policy front, but the bulls are continuously adding positions from the capital side.

As a personal note: any pullback is about “doing it when it comes,” and right now it’s still the same thing—only suitable for short-term trading.

Next week’s focus will be on the Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) jobs data. The market will use it to judge the economic situation and the Fed’s policy direction. If the employment data comes in significantly weaker than expected, it may reduce expectations of further rate hikes and give Bitcoin some breathing room. If the data is strong, the Fed’s hawkish logic would be further reinforced.

What the market is essentially dealing with right now is a battle between long-term allocation capital and short-term policy expectations. The continued inflows into ETFs show that institutions are positioning on dips, but the tightening shadow of macro policy makes short-term funds hesitate to stay in the fight. At the $77,900 level, it’s both a technical crossroads and a battlefield where macro narratives and capital flows collide directly. #BTC #ETH #BTC走势分析

Inflation data has cooled, yet the new Fed chair Warsh pours cold water at Jackson Hole: Why is BTC stuck below $80K?

Fed chair Warsh remains cautious about inflation; rate-cut expectations were dampened, and BTC slipped to $77,897.92.

At the Jackson Hole conference, new Fed chair Kevin Warsh delivered a keynote. The key message is simple: even though recent inflation reports have been easing, he still isn’t “comfortable” with the U.S. inflation trend, and he didn’t send the dovish signal the market wanted.

In plain terms, the market expected him to follow the latest inflation data and imply rate cuts—but instead he chose to stay on hold. After traders listened, they immediately tore up half of the “fast rate cuts this year” script. BTC’s earlier attempts to hold above $80,000 failed several times; after this speech, it pulled back to $77,897.92, down 1.24% over 24 hours. ETH weakened in parallel to $2,445.48, down 1.93%.

Impact on the market
The transmission is direct: Warsh is not dovish → rate-cut expectations cool → the U.S. dollar and Treasury yields strengthen → valuations for risk assets come under pressure → capital flows out of the crypto market, increasing selling pressure on BTC.

- Short term: Liquidity expectations are the core support for this rebound. Once those expectations ease, $80,000 turns from a resistance level into an even harder ceiling. Altcoins are likely to fall even more sharply; ETH’s drop has already exceeded BTC’s, suggesting leveraged capital is retreating.
- Medium term: If subsequent Fed officials collectively stick to this stance, the probability of rate cuts in Q4 could be revised downward. The crypto market may return to a range-bound, choppy pattern, waiting for the next catalyst.

My take
Bearish in the short term. The combination of repeated failed attempts to break above $80,000 and the Fed’s hawkish tone leaves no usable narrative for bulls. Near-term support is around $76,000; if that breaks, sentiment could deteriorate quickly, and ETH may play catch-up down to around $2,300. Only once Warsh—or the subsequent FOMC minutes—signals openness to rate cuts should we talk about a potential turnaround. Risk point: If there’s another weak economic report later this week, the market may pressure the Fed to become dovish, and the selloff may not unfold smoothly.

One-sentence translation: It’s not that money is leaving crypto—rather, the expectation that “cheap money will arrive faster” has been delayed, so the story can’t be told yet; the price has to wait.

The first anti-quantum transaction on the Bitcoin mainnet has been implemented and experimentally validated

Recently, the crypto community has been paying close attention to the real-world progress of the Bitcoin network in the direction of post-quantum security. Multiple reports say that the Bitcoin mainnet has completed an experimental transaction designed with quantum-safe security, aiming to test whether the relevant signature schemes and protection concepts are feasible in the current network environment, and to provide reference for later discussions on long-term upgrades.

The context is that Bitcoin has long relied on classical public-key cryptography systems such as elliptic curve digital signatures. If, in the future, sufficiently powerful quantum computing capabilities emerge, it is theoretically possible to derive private keys or forge signatures from the publicly exposed key information, thereby endangering the security of certain addresses and in-transit transactions. Industry often refers to this potential tipping point as the quantum-related risk window. Although mainstream judgment still holds that large-scale practical attacks have not arrived, once a transaction is broadcast and public-key-related data enter the public network, the risk window objectively exists—so validating defense paths in advance has become an important issue for developers and research institutions.

On core facts, the reports state that a team related to StarkWare completed the first Bitcoin transaction experiment targeted at attacks resistant to quantum threats. The approach was proposed by Avihu Levy, head of the company’s Applications department. The focus is not on immediately changing Bitcoin’s consensus rules, but rather on adding extra protection at the transaction layer to reduce the likelihood that an attacker can exploit publicly available data while the transaction enters the mempool and waits for confirmation. The technical path mentioned using a method akin to “signature grinding”: the system does not simply use the first valid signature; instead, it performs extensive computation to sift for signature forms that are less likely to expose the specific information an attacker needs for the attack. This process is computationally expensive, and generating such a transaction may take several hours. Also, standard Bitcoin nodes typically do not relay transactions in this special format, so the transaction did not follow the usual path through the public mempool. Instead, it was directly packaged through miner channels willing to cooperate. The report says that the mining company MARA used its Slipstream service to include the transaction in a block, enabling it to be confirmed on the mainnet.

Other information summarizes this progress as a successful post-quantum security mainnet test, arguing that it verified the verifiability of quantum-safe signature schemes in the Bitcoin environment, and that it did not cause significant disruption to confirmation time or overall network performance. It’s important to clarify that this is an experimental and early validation; it does not mean the Bitcoin protocol has completed a comprehensive post-quantum upgrade, nor does it mean all users’ assets automatically receive the same level of protection.

In terms of logical breakdown, this can be understood as “a transition validation that is compatible with the existing mainnet,” rather than “a one-shot permanent solution.” StarkWare also emphasized that the protocol layer ultimately still needs more complete post-quantum protection. Before the community reaches broader upgrade consensus, such methods are more like temporary lifeboats: they can demonstrate that it’s possible to explore a certain degree of protection without an immediate hard fork, but they cannot replace long-term protocol improvements. Real-world constraints—high computation cost, limited propagation paths, and reliance on specific miner services—also indicate that for now it is more suitable for research, demonstrations, and small-scope trials, still far from large-scale everyday use.

The impact on the crypto market is more reflected in narratives and infrastructure expectations rather than short-term price signals. On one hand, as the post-quantum topic heats up, it may reinforce market focus on Bitcoin’s long-term security redundancy, development roadmaps, and institutional custody standards, encouraging wallets, exchanges, custodians, and research institutions to evaluate post-quantum migration strategies. On the other hand, the experimental success can help ease extreme sentiment such as “quantum threats are imminent and the existing chain fails immediately,” making the discussion more centered on technical routes, time windows, and upgrade governance. Related progress may also spill over into cryptographic upgrade comparisons in other public chains and layer-2 networks, prompting the industry to more systematically distinguish among three levels: “mainnet experiments,” “protocol upgrades,” and “ecosystem tool adaptation.”

An editor’s observation suggests that interpreting a single mainnet experimental transaction as a fully resolved post-quantum problem for Bitcoin is not accurate. A more reliable view is that the community has moved from paper discussions to observable mainnet validation, showing that transitional protection can still be explored without an immediate fork—while also exposing engineering bottlenecks such as costs, compatibility, and propagation mechanisms. What is worth continuous tracking next is whether similar schemes can reduce computational burdens, whether they can form a more standardized transaction format and gain miner/node support, and whether Bitcoin protocol-layer discussions on post-quantum signatures and address migration will enter a clearer consensus process. The fact remains that the experimental transaction has been confirmed as implemented in the reports. As for its rollout pace and the final security boundaries, they still depend on subsequent technical iterations and governance progress, which should be distinguished from speculation.

content:
比特币主网首笔抗量子交易落地实验验证

近期加密社区关注比特币网络在抗量子方向的实际进展。多份报道称，比特币主网已完成一笔带有量子安全设计的实验性交易，旨在验证相关签名与保护思路在现有网络环境下是否可行，并为后续长期升级讨论提供参考。

事件背景在于，比特币长期依赖椭圆曲线数字签名等经典公钥密码体系。若未来出现足够强大的量子计算能力，理论上可能从已暴露的公钥信息推导私钥或伪造签名，从而威胁部分地址与在途交易安全。业界常将这一潜在临界点称为量子相关风险窗口。尽管当前主流判断仍认为大规模实用攻击尚未到来，但交易一旦广播、公钥相关数据进入公开网络，风险窗口便客观存在，因此提前验证防护路径成为开发者与研究机构的重要课题。

核心事实方面，报道指出StarkWare相关团队完成了首笔面向抗量子攻击目标的比特币交易实验。方案由该公司应用部门负责人Avihu Levy提出，重点并非立刻修改比特币共识规则，而是在交易层面增加额外保护，降低攻击者在交易进入内存池、等待确认期间利用公开数据的可能性。技术路径中提到采用签名磨削一类方法：系统不直接采用首个有效签名，而是通过大量计算筛选更不易暴露关键攻击所需信息的签名形态。该过程计算开销较高，生成一笔此类交易可能耗时数小时。同时，标准比特币节点目前通常不会转发这种特殊格式交易，因此该笔交易并未走常规公共内存池路径，而是经愿意配合的矿工通道直接打包。报道称，矿业公司MARA通过其Slipstream服务将该交易纳入区块，使其在主网得到确认。

另有信息将此进展概括为量子安全相关主网测试成功，认为其验证了量子安全签名方案在比特币环境下的可验证性，且未对确认时间或整体网络性能造成显著冲击。需要明确的是，这属于实验性与早期验证，并不等同于比特币协议已完成抗量子全面升级，也不意味着所有用户资产已自动获得同等防护。

逻辑拆解上，可将此事理解为“兼容现有主网的过渡验证”，而非“一步到位的永久方案”。StarkWare方面亦强调，协议层最终仍需更完整的抗量子保护；在社区形成升级共识前，此类方法更像临时救生措施，能够证明不必立刻硬分叉也能探索一定程度的防护，但不能替代长期协议改进。计算成本高、传播路径受限、依赖特定矿工服务等现实约束，也说明其目前更适合研究、示范与小范围试验，距离大规模日常使用仍有距离。

对加密市场的影响路径，更多体现在叙事与基础设施预期，而非短期价格信号。一方面，抗量子议题升温，可能强化市场对比特币长期安全冗余、开发路线图与机构托管标准的关注，推动钱包、交易所、托管方和研究机构评估后量子迁移策略；另一方面，实验成功有助于缓和“量子威胁迫在眉睫、现有链立即失效”的极端情绪，使讨论更聚焦于技术路径、时间窗口与升级治理。相关进展也可能外溢到其他公链与二层网络的密码学升级比较，促使行业更系统地区分“主网实验”“协议升级”和“生态工具适配”三个层次。

编辑观察认为，把单笔主网实验交易解读为比特币抗量子问题已彻底解决，并不准确；更稳妥的判断是：社区已从纸面讨论迈向可观测的主网验证，证明在不立即分叉的前提下仍可探索过渡防护，同时暴露了成本、兼容性与传播机制等工程瓶颈。后续值得持续跟踪的，是类似方案能否降低计算负担、能否形成更标准化的交易格式与矿工/节点支持，以及比特币协议层关于后量子签名与地址迁移的讨论是否进入更明确的共识进程。事实是实验交易已在报道中被确认落地；至于其推广节奏与最终安全边界，仍取决于后续技术迭代与治理进展，需与推测保持区分。

title: Crypto Market Update: BTC Consolidates Near $80K as ETFs, Rates and Regulation Set the Tone
subTitle:
Bitcoin enters the new KST day consolidating near the $80,000 area after a sharp late-August rebound. The market is balancing two opposing forces: renewed institutional demand through spot ETFs and a less friendly macro backdrop after hawkish Jackson Hole commentary lifted Treasury yields and weighed on bitcoin-linked risk assets.

ETF flows remain the strongest constructive signal. Recent market data showed U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs extending an eight-session buying streak, with roughly $2.8 billion added during the run. Ether ETFs followed the same direction, adding more than $1 billion over their own streak. That combination matters because simultaneous BTC and ETH inflows usually support broader liquidity, first into large-cap altcoins and then into higher-beta narratives.

Regulation is also keeping sentiment supported. The SEC's August crypto-asset proposal and related statements point toward a more defined U.S. framework, while the CLARITY Act debate remains a key autumn market-structure event. Stablecoins continue to attract policy attention as governments and payment firms link tokenized dollars with settlement, Treasury-bill demand and global payment rails.

Still, the rally is not free of risk. A higher-rate message from the Fed can cool risk appetite quickly, especially after a fast move and heavy liquidations. Traders should watch whether BTC can hold the $80,000 zone, whether ETH keeps relative strength, whether ETF inflows persist into month-end, and whether funding rates stay orderly.

The market backdrop is constructive but tactical: liquidity has improved, policy visibility is better, and institutional demand is active, yet macro rates remain the pressure point that can decide whether the breakout extends or pauses.

📈 What Are Higher Highs & Lower Lows?
Understanding Higher Highs (HH) and Lower Lows (LL) is one of the basics of reading market structure in crypto.
🟢 Higher High (HH)
A Higher High forms when price moves above its previous swing high.
➡️ HH = Stronger upward market structure
For example, if $BTC , ETH, or SOL keeps forming Higher Highs and Higher Lows, it can indicate a developing uptrend.
🔴 Lower Low (LL)
A Lower Low forms when price falls below its previous swing low.
➡️ LL = Stronger downward market structure
If BTC, ETH, or $SOL repeatedly forms Lower Lows and Lower Highs, it can indicate a bearish market structure.
📌 Simple Example
Uptrend:
Higher High → Higher Low → Higher High → Higher Low 📈
Downtrend:
Lower Low → Lower High → Lower Low → Lower High 📉
⚠️ Why Does It Matter?
Market structure helps traders understand whether buyers or sellers are showing more strength.
A single HH or LL doesn't automatically confirm a trend. Consider support/resistance, volume, liquidity, and the broader market structure.
📚 Key Takeaway:
HH + HL = Bullish Structure
LL + LH = Bearish Structure
You can apply this concept when analyzing BTC, $ETH , and SOL charts.

Sberbank plans to accept USDT, BTC, and ETH as loan collateral, widening a crack in the sanctions framework.

Sberbank isn’t a small bank—it’s Russia’s largest state-owned bank, with assets accounting for about one-third of the entire Russian banking industry. It plans to allow customers to use USDT, BTC, and ETH as collateral to borrow fiat or stablecoins. In plain terms: Russia’s biggest traditional financial institution is officially treating crypto assets as “eligible collateral.” The backdrop is that, under sanctions, Russia’s cross-border payments have been cut off via SWIFT. Companies and individuals are using USDT as a trade conduit, and the demand is already there—so the bank is simply taking the next step.

One-sentence translation: In Russia, crypto has shifted from a “gray-market tool” to an asset recognized by banks—this is a government-level compliance signal.

Market impact
- Short term: A sentiment tailwind. The transmission path is very direct: Russian-linked capital is a large holder of USDT—bank endorsement increases USDT circulation demand—Tether issues more (mints) → boosting stablecoin purchasing power in the market, which indirectly supports BTC and ETH prices. - Medium term: The real impact lies in the regulatory landscape. The G7 has been trying to choke off Russian crypto channels; now, with a state-owned bank openly integrating, it forces the U.S. Treasury and the EU to make a choice: either tighten oversight of Tether (the biggest tail risk for USDT), or accept the reality on the ground. Short-term bullish, but don’t get carried away. SBI smashes $270 million to secure a 20% stake in Ajaib: has the retail-on-ramp in Asia finally been opened?

Japanese financial giant SBI invests $270 million in Indonesian brokerage Ajaib—another chunk of bandwidth for the Asian crypto entry.

SBI Holdings announced a $270 million investment in Indonesia’s investment platform Ajaib, taking a 20% stake. Ajaib isn’t a pure exchange; it puts stocks, funds, crypto, and stablecoins into a single app, and also provides OTC settlement services for institutional clients. In plain terms, what SBI is targeting is the young retail segment in Indonesia’s population of 270 million that still hasn’t opened accounts—traditional brokerages can’t really chew through that market, and a strategy combining crypto with traditional assets may be able to. Over the past couple of years, SBI has been very aggressive in positioning itself in on-chain assets; this deal is another piece in its Asian map.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment is a positive. BTC is now at $77,689.99 and ETH at $2,435.51, both falling (24h -1.98% and -2.65%). This kind of news may not hold up the price action, but it does show institutional capital hasn’t been idle—during the dip, there are still people putting real money into the sector.
- Medium term: more meaningful. Traditional Asian finance keeps increasing its commitment to crypto infrastructure, meaning the channels for the next wave of retail entrants are being built ahead of time. The Indonesia + Japan combination is aimed squarely at the incremental market with the biggest demographic dividend. Stablecoins and OTC settlement are placed at the core, indicating that institutional demand here is very real.

My view

Iranian officials have made their position clear: any rival trying to reopen the Strait of Hormuz will be prevented. This strait carries about 20 million barrels of oil per day, accounting for two-tenths of global oil trade. Of course, “blocking” sounds easy but doing it is hard—yet the escalation itself is the variable: when oil prices swing, inflation expectations come back, the Fed’s rate-cut window gets squeezed again, and the funding chain for risk assets breaks. The transmission path is straightforward: geopolitical conflict → higher oil prices → higher inflation expectations → tighter liquidity expectations → BTC sell pressure.

- Short term: purely bearish. BTC is already falling (24h -2.35% to $77,589.98), ETH is down even more (-2.63% to $2,434.89), XRP -2.85%. - Medium term: if the blockade is only a verbal threat with no real action, the impact may be digested in 1–2 weeks. But as soon as oil shipping is genuinely disrupted, a spike in oil prices will strengthen the “stagflation” narrative, suppressing overall risk appetite for the rest of the year.

Bearish in the short term—no disguising it. BTC is at $77,589; the level to watch below is the psychological $75,000. A break could send it straight to prior lows. Iran threatens to blockade the Strait of Hormuz—global oil prices and shipping are in turmoil, and BTC and ETH get cut too.

Official Iranian statements: If anyone wants to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, they’ll be stopped. This strait is a key passage for roughly 20% of the world’s crude oil shipments. The moment the words came out, the market’s first reaction was a surge in expectations for higher oil prices plus a broad retreat from risk assets. In plain terms, this is a signal of escalation in geopolitical confrontation, and the room for diplomatic negotiations is actually squeezed.

- Medium term: If tension around the strait persists, higher oil prices will boost inflation expectations. The Federal Reserve’s rate-cut path gets thrown off, and tighter liquidity becomes a sustained drag on crypto prices. Sideline money won’t rush in under this kind of environment.

At Jackson Hole, Warsh’s first home address was even more hawkish than the market expected. Three points: the six-month PCE is still 4.1%, financial conditions are “not really tight,” and he directly rejected forward guidance. The moment the news hit, September rate-hike odds jumped to 50%. - Short term: BTC slid from around $78,700 to $77,574.01. ETH was at $2,434.28, with both down more than 2%. ETFs shifted from buying to selling—$201.9 million outflow—which is the first material turn in fund flows in this round of pullback, more worth watching than the price move itself.

Bearish in the short term. The U.S. BTC spot ETF has ended nine straight days of net buying, with a daily net outflow; yet ETH ETF continues to pull in money.

On August 28, the U.S. BTC spot ETF recorded a net outflow of $202 million, breaking the momentum of nine consecutive trading days of continuous buying since August 17, totaling about $3.0 billion. On the same day, ETH spot ETFs recorded a net inflow of $102 million—funds didn’t leave, they just switched tracks. BTC is currently quoted at $77,580.71, down 2.32% over 24 hours; ETH at $2,434.45, down 2.56%.

Market impact
- Short term: The momentum behind BTC’s continuous buying has been interrupted. The most likely to wobble is the short-term capital that just chased in; there’s a high probability of near-term price pressure.
ETH’s continued inflows are a bright hedging point, but its scale is only one-third of BTC’s inflow phase, so it can’t prop up the broader market.
- Medium term: A single day of outflows doesn’t necessarily signal a trend reversal. The $3.0 billion buy base over nine days is still there. What to watch next is the coming two or three days—only continuous outflows would be a sign of institutional withdrawal. An isolated outflow day looks more like profit-taking.

Slightly bearish in the short term. If BTC fails to hold around $77,580.71, the support of the prior consolidation range below should be considered effective. 短线视角来看，4这个位置很微妙。如果它能放量突破0.01759并站稳，那下一个目标可以看0.02附近，盈亏比大概1:2.5。但我的建议是别追这个位置，等回踩0.0155-0.016这个区间再看，止损放在0.0142（近8根K线支撑0.01229太远了，不现实），第一目标0.0175，算下来RR差不多1:2。交易失效条件很明确：如果它跌回0.014以下且放量，那这波拉升就是假突破，果断认错离场。

龙虾更夸张，0.0728，涨了29.19%，但你看它的24h低点0.03155——这币今天振幅超过130%！现在价格在区间96%处，基本就是贴着高点0.0745在走。资金费率0.115%，比4还高，说明市场情绪已经亢奋到极点。说实话这种走势我最怕，冲高回落留长上影的概率非常大。

我的思路是：龙虾这个位置偏空思路比偏多更有性价比。如果它冲不上0.0745且出现15分钟级别的放量下跌，可以轻仓试空，止损0.078，第一目标0.065，RR大概1:2。注意啊，这纯粹是短线博弈，中线我根本不敢碰这种振幅的币（上次吃了个大亏就是因为追高类似的走势，手动狗头）。

CLO倒是有点意思，涨幅26.2%但资金费率只有0.0142%，说明这波拉升不是靠合约杠杆推的，是实打实的现货买盘。当前价格0.1221，距24h高点0.127就差4%，支撑在0.116。这个币的叙事是跨链清算层，概念还行，但22M的量能说实话一般。如果它能回踩0.116-0.118不破，可以看多方向，止损0.112，目标0.127，RR≈1:2.2。失效条件：跌破0.112且收盘站不回去，那就说明这波行情结束了。

大盘方面，BTC 77,573，24h跌了2.55%，ETH也是绿的。恐惧贪婪指数35，市场整体偏谨慎。但我反而觉得这种时候山寨币的独立行情更值得关注——大盘横盘的时候资金会去找热点，今天的热点就是4和龙虾。

最后说一句，现在这个市场情绪下，追高是最危险的动作。恐惧指数35意味着大部分人都在观望，但涨幅榜上这些币已经涨了30%+，说明少部分人已经在赚钱了。我的建议是：要么等回调再进，要么就别碰。别看着别人赚钱就眼红，保住本金比什么都重要。

Metaplanet transfers 3,000 BTC to Coinbase Prime: not a sell-off, it’s accounting

The largest BTC-listed-company holder in Japan has transferred $237 million worth of Bitcoin to an exchange for custody. There are concerns about short-term selling pressure, but the outlook is neutral-to-slightly positive in the long run.

Metaplanet transferred 3,000 BTC—worth about $237 million at current prices—into Coinbase Prime. Currently, BTC is at $77,643.01, down 2.49% over the past 24 hours. Such transfers are usually interpreted in two ways: (1) preparations to sell (sending coins out to the exchange to sell), or (2) switching to institutional-grade custody (in-exchange custody is often used for collateral, borrowing, and derivatives hedging).

Metaplanet is Japan’s MicroStrategy. It follows a debt-issuance-and-buy-BTC route, and has been using BTC for capital operations—making the latter interpretation clearly more likely.

Impact on the market
- Short term: On-chain monitoring will treat a “large transfer to an exchange” as a sell-pressure signal, so sentiment is slightly bearish. However, this transfer is only a fraction of Metaplanet’s holdings—it’s not a full liquidation. BTC itself is already down 2.49%. At most, this news gives bears an extra excuse; it isn’t the main cause of the drop.
- Medium term: When institutions move coins from cold wallets into Prime custody, it actually indicates that BTC is becoming a balance-sheet tool that can be used as collateral. This is an inevitable step toward institutionalization—and it’s good for the industry.

My take
I think this news is neutral-to-bullish. The logic is simple: if the intent were truly to dump BTC, choosing Coinbase Prime wouldn’t make sense—sending to a hot wallet would be easier and more efficient. The custody nature of Prime points to financing and collateral use, which is a prerequisite for Metaplanet to keep leveraging up to buy more BTC.

In the short term, BTC is likely to consolidate around $77,643.01. Support to watch is around $76,000. As long as it doesn’t break down on heavy volume, the market will likely forget this transfer within a few hours. The real factor determining direction is macro liquidity—not a single company’s transfer record.

Metaplanet把3000枚BTC转进Coinbase Prime：不是砸盘，是在做账

日本最大BTC上市公司持有人把2.37亿美元比特币转入交易所托管，短期抛压担忧，长期偏中性。

Metaplanet把3000枚BTC、按当前价格算约2.37亿美元，转入Coinbase Prime。目前BTC报$77,643.01，24小时跌2.49%。这种转账通常有两种解读：一是准备卖出（打交易所出货），二是换成机构级托管（场内托管通常用于抵押、借债、做衍生品对冲）。Metaplanet是日本版MicroStrategy，走的是发债买币的路线，一直在用BTC做资本运作，后者概率明显更大。

对市场的影响
- 短期：链上监控会把“大额转入交易所”当成抛压信号，情绪面偏空，但这笔只占Metaplanet持仓的零头级别，不是清仓动作。BTC本身已经跌2.49%，这个消息最多是给空头多一个借口，不是下跌主因。
- 中期：机构把币从冷钱包搬进Prime托管，恰恰说明BTC正在变成可抵押的资产负债表工具。这是机构化的必经之路，对行业是好事。

我的判断
我判断这条消息是中性偏多。理由很简单：如果是真要砸盘卖币，不会选Coinbase Prime，直接打热钱包更省事。Prime的托管属性指向融资和抵押用途，这是Metaplanet继续加杠杆买币的前置动作。短期BTC在$77,643.01附近震荡，下方关注7.6万美元一线支撑，只要不放量跌破，这个转账消息最多消化几个小时就会被市场遗忘。真正决定方向的还是宏观流动性，不是单一公司的转账记录。

The White House Teleprompter Operator Paid More Than $170,000 to Settle a Prediction-Market Probe

The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) has recently disclosed a regulatory settlement related to a prediction market. A former White House staffer who was responsible for operating teleprompters allegedly used advance access to presidential speech information to time bets precisely on a contracts platform for prediction markets. The investigation was ultimately closed after the individual paid a fine and remitted related profits. The case again put the boundary between “insider advantage from a job position” and event contracts that can be publicly traded at the center of market discussion.

On key facts, Gabriel Perez agreed to pay a $65,000 civil penalty to the CFTC and to forfeit more than $107,000 in profits, for a total payment of more than $172,000. He also accepted a three-year trading ban. He denied the regulator’s allegations that he misappropriated nonpublic information and profited on the prediction-trading platform Kalshi. In its news release, the regulator said the penalty was significantly reduced in light of his cooperation with the investigation. A cease-and-desist order states that, as a White House employee, Perez knew that information he accessed in the course of his work was confidential and could not be disclosed to people outside the White House.

The background traces to abnormal trading detected on the platform side. Public reporting shows that in March, Kalshi detected unusual trades and reported them to regulators. At the time, the White House said the implicated employee had been placed on unpaid administrative leave. Perez is suspected of trading contract ranges roughly from December 2025 to February 2026, with his activities concentrated almost entirely on sports and contracts related to Trump— including bets on content that the president might say in certain settings. The regulator said he generally received the speech script about an hour before the speech. A Kalshi enforcement executive publicly stated that the platform had detected rule-violating trades, emphasizing that regardless of identity, violations of platform rules or federal law must be held to account. The CFTC treats prediction-market platforms like these as derivatives exchanges under its jurisdiction, meaning a regulatory framework prohibiting the misuse of nonpublic information may apply.

In terms of the underlying logic, the controversy is not about whether one can bet on the publicly known outcomes of speeches. Rather, it is whether an insider converted draft script information—still unreleased and obtained through their job—into a trading advantage. So-called “mention-type” contracts allow users to bet on whether public figures will use particular words or phrases in contexts such as speeches. For someone who already has the text in advance, the uncertainty of the outcome is dramatically reduced, and an information gap may turn into unfair profit. Choosing a settlement, not admitting to the allegations while paying a fine and accepting a ban, is a common resolution path in regulatory practice: it shortens procedures, hardens compliance signals, and simultaneously preserves the respondent’s space to deny the allegations. The key is to separate confirmed facts from inferences: what has been verified here is that the investigation was settled, the amounts and ban duration, and the platform reporting and cooperation. What has not been separately confirmed in this case is how prevalent similar conduct is across the industry.

As for the impact on the ecosystem related to crypto and broader digital assets, the transmission is more along the lines of “rule expectations—platform governance—product design,” rather than a single price shock. In recent months, platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket have seen rising popularity, allowing users to trade contracts involving sports, elections, and a variety of event outcomes. As concerns about insider trading have intensified, platforms may continue strengthening requirements around employer information disclosure, monitoring for abnormal behavior, and transferring leads to law-enforcement agencies. At the legislative level, some lawmakers have already proposed motions to restrict certain betting activity, and the White House has warned employees not to use confidential information to place bets on such platforms. If compliance requirements move upward, the short term could mean higher operational and participation costs and reduced activity for certain information-sensitive contracts; in the medium to long term, it may help raise platform credibility so that more compliance-minded capital is willing to engage with event contracts under clear rules. In the crypto industry, mechanism design related to prediction, information aggregation, and governance voting may also borrow more from traditional derivatives markets’ standards for preventing nonpublic-information abuse.

The editor’s assessment is: at the enforcement and resolution level, this case has been relatively complete—regulators finished the investigation, the parties settled with a fine and a ban, and the platform actively monitored and cooperated, forming a verifiable chain of facts. Of greater reference value to market participants is this: prediction markets need to expand capacity, but they must prove they can effectively identify and block conduct that exploits nonpublic information from job positions. Otherwise, trust losses may outweigh the surface-level boom created by short-term increases in trading activity. How subsequent legislative language will be implemented, and whether more similar cases will be collectively disclosed, remains a matter for observation, and it would be inappropriate to extrapolate from a single case to draw an industry-wide conclusion.

content:
白宫提词器操作员支付逾17万美元了结预测市场调查

美国商品期货交易委员会近日披露一起与预测市场相关的监管了结结果。一名曾在白宫负责提词器操作的工作人员，因涉嫌利用提前接触的总统演讲信息，在事件合约平台上精准择时下注，最终以缴纳罚金并上缴相关获利的方式结束调查。此事把“职务信息优势”与可公开交易的事件合约之间的边界，再次推到市场讨论的中心。

核心事实方面，加布里埃尔·佩雷斯同意向美国商品期货交易委员会缴纳6.5万美元罚金，并上缴逾10.7万美元获利，合计支付逾17.2万美元；同时接受为期三年的交易禁令。他不承认监管机构关于其盗用内幕信息、在预测交易平台Kalshi上牟利的指控。监管机构在新闻稿中称，鉴于其配合调查，本次罚金已做大幅减免。相关停止违法行为令指出，身为白宫工作人员，佩雷斯明知工作中接触的信息属于机密，不得向白宫以外人员泄露。

背景脉络可追溯到平台侧的异常交易发现。公开报道显示，Kalshi在3月监测到异常交易并上报监管机构；白宫方面当时表示涉事雇员已被安排无薪行政休假。佩雷斯涉嫌交易区间约在2025年12月至2026年2月，其活动几乎集中于体育及与特朗普相关的合约，包括押注总统在特定场合讲话中可能出现的内容。监管机构称，他一般能在演讲前约一小时拿到讲稿。Kalshi执法负责人公开表示，平台已监测到违规交易，强调无论身份如何，违反平台规则或联邦法律均须承担责任。美国商品期货交易委员会将此类预测市场平台视作其管辖下的衍生品交易所，因此可适用禁止滥用非公开信息的监管框架。

逻辑拆解上，争议焦点并非“能不能对公开演讲结果下注”，而是内部人员是否把尚未公开、因职务获得的讲稿信息转化为交易优势。所谓提及类合约，允许用户押注公众人物是否在演讲等场合使用特定词句；对提前掌握文本的人而言，结果不确定性被显著压缩，信息差可能演变为不公平获利。选择和解、不承认指控但支付罚金并接受禁令，是监管实践中常见的了结路径：缩短程序、固化合规信号，同时保留当事人对指控的否认空间。需要把事实与推断分开：已确认的是调查了结、金额构成、禁令期限与平台上报配合；尚未被本案单独证实的，是同类行为在全行业的普遍程度。

对加密及广义数字资产相关生态的影响，更多沿“规则预期—平台治理—产品设计”传导，而非单一价格冲击。过去一段时间，Kalshi、Polymarket等平台热度上升，用户可对体育、选举及各类事件结果参与合约。内幕交易担忧升温后，平台可能继续强化雇主信息披露、异常行为监控与向执法部门移交线索；立法层面已有议员提出约束部分押注行为的动议，白宫也警告员工不得利用机密信息在此类场所下注。若合规要求上移，短期或提高运营与参与成本，并压缩部分信息敏感型合约的活跃度；中长期则有助于抬升平台公信力，使更重视合规的资金愿意在清晰规则下接触事件合约。加密行业里与预测、信息聚合、治理投票相关的机制设计，也可能更多借鉴传统衍生品市场对非公开信息的防控标准。

编辑判断是：本案在处置层面已相对完整，监管完成调查、当事人以罚金加禁令了结、平台主动监控并配合，构成可核验的事实链条。对市场参与者更有参考价值的，是预测市场要扩容，必须证明能有效识别并阻断利用职务非公开信息的行为；否则信任损耗可能超过短期交易活跃带来的表面繁荣。后续立法文本如何落地、是否还有更多类似案件被集中披露，仍属观察项，不宜用单一个案外推为全行业结论。

title: Crypto Market Update: ETF Demand and U.S. Policy Keep BTC and ETH in Focus
subTitle:
Bitcoin and Ethereum remain the center of the crypto market narrative as the new week approaches. Recent reports show investors returning to spot Bitcoin ETFs, with a multi-day inflow streak that reflects renewed demand for alternatives to the dollar and other fiat assets. Ether ETFs have also logged sustained inflows, which matters because simultaneous BTC and ETH demand often improves liquidity across major altcoins.

The macro backdrop is less simple. Treasury yields and Fed policy expectations remain important for risk assets, and a higher-for-longer rate message can quickly slow speculative momentum. That leaves Bitcoin's recent move around the $80,000 area as a tactical test rather than a clean one-way breakout.

Policy clarity is another major theme. The SEC's August proposal for crypto assets would create a tailored securities offering framework for certain crypto investment contracts. The market is also watching U.S. market-structure debate, including the CLARITY Act path into September. Better rules can support institutional participation, but details still matter for token issuance, exchange compliance and DeFi activity.

Stablecoins remain one of the strongest structural stories. They are increasingly discussed as payment rails, Treasury-bill demand channels and always-on settlement infrastructure, not just trading collateral. Any bank, regulator or issuer update in this area can affect liquidity expectations.

For traders, the clean watchlist is BTC near $80,000, ETH relative strength, ETF inflow persistence, funding rates and fresh policy headlines. The setup is constructive, but macro rates and crowded leverage can still turn momentum into volatility.

Solana Inflation Halved, Proposal Approved: SOL’s Future New Supply Suddenly Cuts in Half

Solana validators voted in favor of the proposal, reducing the annual inflation reduction rate from 15% to 30%. As a result, the amount of new SOL being minted drops sharply—directly benefiting SOL.

In plain terms: SOL will be “saving” instead of over-issuing. Previously, Solana’s inflation rate decreased each year at 15%. After validators approved this change, the reduction speed is increased to 30%. That means the amount of additional SOL minted each year going forward will be much lower than originally planned. Note: this isn’t changing the long-term inflation floor—the endpoint stays the same. What changes is the speed to reach it: it’s like slowing down has been replaced with faster running.

One-sentence translation: Same destination, but the route is cut in half—future sell pressure tightens earlier.

Market impact
- Short term: A tighter supply outlook is a textbook bullish catalyst. On the day the news was released, the SOL price was $105.46, up 2.47% within 24 hours—outperforming BTC by 1.01% and ETH by 0.96%. The market is already voting with its feet. That said, such bullish news often moves “ahead of expectations.” Watch out for quick profit-taking after the rollout.
- Mid term: With disinflation plus staking yields still attractive, SOL’s real staking return becomes more compelling, which may continue to pull staking capital from other PoS chains. This also sets an example for other high-inflation chains: communities can solve inflation themselves.

My take
Clearly bullish. Supply-side contraction is one of the few narratives that can hold without external inflow—fewer new coins being issued means that, with the same level of demand, the price’s central tendency naturally shifts upward. If SOL holds above $105, the trend looks healthy. If it pulls back toward around $100 and can defend that level, it would be strong support and a validation area. The main risk lies with the overall market: if BTC weakens around $78,266, SOL likely won’t be able to stay completely independent—that’s the biggest variable.

One-sentence summary: Fundamentals are bullish, but don’t ignore the market’s mood.

Jackson Hole Ends: Warsh’s Debut Turns Hawkish, Markets Shift From Waiting for Rate Cuts to Fearing Rate Hikes

The Fed’s annual event wraps up with Warsh’s first hawkish showing as the new chair. Rate-cut expectations collapse, and fears of rate hikes move in.

At Jackson Hole, Warsh made his first appearance as the Fed’s new chief, with a clearly hawkish tone. The market had expected discussions on the timing of rate cuts, but instead heard signals that monetary policy could be tightened further. In plain terms, the whole script flips: it goes from “when will they cut” to “will they hike.” Global assets are highly sensitive to this wording, with risk assets taking the first hit.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Bearish. The transmission is straightforward—rate-hike expectations rise → U.S. Treasury yields move up → the dollar strengthens → pressure builds on risk-asset valuations. Crypto, as the most liquidity-sensitive asset, sees sell pressure arrive first. BTC is currently at $78,156.14 (up just +1.03% over 24h). After the hawkish news lands, this upside is unlikely to hold. ETH at $2,453.65 (+1.31%) has greater elasticity, meaning pullbacks could be harsher. If ETF flows turn into outflows, they directly drain BTC’s buy-side support.
- Medium term: Higher rates staying in place for longer → a systematic decline in risk appetite → altcoin liquidity shrinks further, with capital concentrating toward the top.

My take
Bearish—no sugarcoating. Warsh’s debut being hawkish shows this isn’t a trial balloon; it’s a policy tone signal. For BTC in the short term, watch the $76,000 support zone. A break below would open room for further downside. Resistance is at $80,000 for any rebound. ETH follows BTC but with amplified volatility; around $2,380 is a key level. Risk point: if subsequent inflation data weakens, the hawkish stance could soften and the market may repair quickly—but that would come after the data speaks. For now, treat it as bearish.

美联储年会收尾，新主席Warsh鹰派首秀，降息预期崩了，加息恐惧来了。

Jackson Hole年会上，Warsh以美联储新掌门身份首次亮相，基调明显偏鹰。市场原本预期的是讨论降息节奏，结果听到的是可能进一步收紧货币政策的信号。说白了，剧本整个反过来了：从“什么时候降”变成“会不会加”。全球资产对这套措辞极其敏感，风险资产首当其冲。

- 中期：高利率维持更久→市场风险偏好系统性下降→山寨币流动性进一步萎缩，资金向头部集中。

Jackson Hole wraps up: Warsh makes his debut and turns hawkish—markets start worrying about rate hikes, not cuts

Fed chairman Warsh turns hawkish at Jackson Hole, reigniting concerns about further rate hikes, which is bearish for both BTC and ETH.

Jackson Hole has ended. The biggest focus for the entire event was the first appearance of the newly appointed Fed chair, Warsh. He didn’t give the easing signals the market wanted—instead, he clearly went hawkish, implying monetary policy could tighten further, and even leaving the door open to rate hikes. This statement directly shattered the market’s prior hopes for a rate-cut path. To be honest, Warsh’s opening tone is crucial—it’s basically telling the market: don’t expect money to get cheap anytime soon.

One-sentence translation: The market was hoping for rate cuts, but what it got was a warning that hikes may be coming.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Liquidity expectations tighten, and risk assets take the first hit. BTC is now at $78,156.14, down 1.03% in 24h; ETH at $2,453.65, down 1.31%. This pullback isn’t severe, suggesting the market is still in the digestion phase and that the real pressure may not have been fully released. The crypto market is extremely sensitive to rate expectations—hawkish statements usually hit valuations first and then sentiment.
- Medium term: If rate hikes truly materialize, on-chain activity and funding conditions will both come under pressure, and liquidity for altcoins will worsen further. Watch upcoming Non-Farm Payrolls and CPI data—that’s the key checkpoint for validating just how hawkish Warsh really is.

My view
I’m bearish. $78,156 isn’t a solid bottom; if it breaks down within the next 12 hours, downside space will open up. ETH at $2,453 is also hanging in the balance. The 24-hour drop of 1.31% looks mild, but ETH’s sensitivity to liquidity has historically been higher than BTC’s. Once rate-hike expectations heat up, the decline is likely to amplify. The only scenario that could turn things bullish is if subsequent data weakens enough to force Warsh to backtrack—but in the short term, don’t count on it.

Metaplanet transfers 3,000 BTC to Coinbase Prime: not a sell-off—could it actually be good news?

One of Japan’s largest publicly listed companies holding BTC has moved 3,000 bitcoins into Coinbase Prime, and the market is speculating about what it plans to do.

Metaplanet transferred 3,000 BTC (about $237 million) to Coinbase Prime. Note that this is an institutional custody service, not coins sent directly to an exchange to be sold. Such moves are usually for staking, lending/borrowing, or getting ready for future financing. Metaplanet has been following MicroStrategy’s playbook: stockpile coins, raise funds, then stockpile again. Moving to Coinbase Prime looks more like a preparatory capital-management step.

One-sentence translation: the coins aren’t being sold—but the groundwork is being laid for “putting the coins to work.”

Market impact
- Short term: Sentiment gets jolted. Large on-chain transfers of BTC to exchange-linked addresses cause some people to panic first. BTC is already trading weakly at $77,643.01 (24h -2.49%), so this kind of news can be amplified as “institutions are about to dump.” But Coinbase Prime ≠ an exchange hot wallet, so the odds of a dump are lower.
- Medium term: If Metaplanet really uses this batch for staking or collateralized financing, it effectively demonstrates to the market an institutional path of “earning yield while holding + adding leverage.” In the longer run, this is an incremental strategy.

My take
Slightly bullish on balance. At its core, this transfer is treasury management, not a sell-off signal. At the $77,643 level, BTC has already been drifting lower on low volume; the real variable is macro, not this single transfer. If Metaplanet later announces financing or a staking/collateral plan, that would confirm a positive catalyst; if on-chain activity shows further transfers to exchange hot wallets, then we’re talking about something else. ETH $2,436.19 (24h -2.81%) moves in tandem—there’s no independent logic.

- Direction: Neutral—the event itself doesn’t drive direction

【Quantum computing threats have moved from paper to reality, and the ETH ecosystem faces an underestimated uphill battle】

Yesterday, Bitcoin and Ethereum both released plans for post-quantum migration, and the market barely reacted. Trading was slow, and the price chart just drew an uninteresting flat line.

But I have to say, this signal was seriously overlooked.

In that CoinDesk report, there’s a hardcore detail: an Anthropic model reduced the computational workload required to break a certain post-quantum signature scheme by 67 million times. That happened last month.

What does a 67 million times reduction mean? It’s like something that used to take 100 years of computation can now be done in a matter of seconds.

Ripple is already “quantum-hardening” the XRP Ledger. On the Ledger side, they fixed a transaction replacement vulnerability in an older version of an app—no money was lost, but it exposed a very real issue: those older signature schemes on-chain are basically paper-thin in the face of quantum computers.

So what about ETH?

The migration plan is out, and it sounds grand. But if you think a layer deeper—how many DeFi protocols, how many NFT contracts, how many multisig wallets are on Ethereum that still rely on the signature algorithms that now seem “good enough”? These contracts can’t be patched the way you update a mobile app.

Many cannot be upgraded.

What does this mean from a business logic standpoint?

First, the first wave of impact isn’t only about on-chain asset security, but about every scenario that relies on “proving ownership with private keys”—your ETH, your ERC-20 tokens, your NFTs. The day quantum computing becomes mature, all historical transaction records signed with ECDSA may be traceably cracked.

Second is the infrastructure layer. Wallets, exchanges, and custody providers all have to keep two systems running in parallel during the signature algorithm migration. The costs aren’t trivial, and the window period is long.

I’m not saying quantum computers can crack Ethereum tomorrow. But the signal is already very clear: this migration isn’t a matter of “whether to do it,” but “who finishes first and avoids the pitfalls.”

The real Alpha worth watching isn’t whether ETH is going up or down right now—it's which infrastructure providers and which on-chain protocols can survive this hard quantum-migration battle and do well.

This is something that will be very interesting in the future.

Which kind of project do you think can get a head start in this migration wave? Let’s discuss in the comments.

【量子计算威胁已从纸面走向现实，ETH生态面临一个被低估的硬仗】

昨天Bitcoin和Ethereum同时发布了抗量子迁移计划，市场几乎没什么反应。成交清淡，K线画着无聊的横线。

但我得说，这个信号被严重忽视了。

CoinDesk那条消息里有个硬核细节：Anthropic的模型把破解一种后量子签名方案所需的工作量削减了6700万倍。上个月的事。

6700万倍什么概念？相当于原来要跑一百年的计算，现在几秒钟搞定。

Ripple已经在给XRP Ledger做量子加固了，Ledger那边修复了一个老版本app的交易替换漏洞——虽然没丢钱，但暴露了一个很现实的问题：链上那些老旧签名方案，在量子计算机面前就是纸糊的。

那ETH这边呢？

迁移计划出来了，听起来很宏大。但你往深里想一层——以太坊上有多少DeFi协议、多少NFT合约、多少多签钱包，用的还是现在看起来"够用"的签名算法？这些合约可不像升级手机APP那样打个补丁就完事。

很多是没法升级的。

从商业逻辑上看，这意味着什么？

第一波受影响的不只是链上资产安全，而是所有"用私钥证明所有权"的场景——你的ETH、你的ERC-20代币、你的NFT。量子计算机成熟的那天，历史上所有用ECDSA签名的交易记录都可能被追溯破解。

第二波是基础设施层。钱包、交易所、托管服务商，都得在签名算法迁移期间保持两套系统并行运转。成本不小，窗口期很长。

我不是说量子计算机明天就能破解以太坊。但信号已经很清楚了：这场迁移不是"要不要做"，而是"谁先做完谁少踩坑"。

真正值得关注的Alpha不是ETH现在涨还是跌——而是哪些基础设施服务商、哪些链上协议能在量子迁移这场硬仗里活下来、活得好。

这东西未来会很有意思。

你看好哪类项目能在这波迁移里拿到先手？评论区聊聊。

Visa partners with Upbit’s parent to develop stablecoin payments: not issuing tokens, but taking the settlement gateway for AI ecommerce

Visa and Dunamu explore stablecoin payments and remittances—traditional payment giants officially move in to grab the Crypto settlement market.

Visa announced a partnership with Upbit parent company Dunamu, with two focus areas: stablecoin payments and remittances, plus AI business scenarios. Notably, OUSD proposed by Open Standard is on the assessment shortlist, but it’s only one of the candidate projects and not decided yet. In plain terms, Visa doesn’t plan to issue its own stablecoin; it’s selecting a compliant on-chain settlement route to connect its payment network with Crypto infrastructure. Upbit is South Korea’s largest exchange—Dunamu has both traffic and licenses—while Visa has a global merchant network. Each side gets what it needs.

Market impact
Short term: This kind of partnership news is sentiment-positive, but it has limited direct pull on mainstream coins like BTC and ETH. Currently, BTC is $78,199.56 (24h +0.80%), ETH is $2,457.6 (+0.83%). The price action is steady, suggesting the market isn’t treating it as a breakout catalyst to trade aggressively. The real beneficiaries are stablecoin-related concepts and payment-sector projects, where a wave of coordinated momentum is expected.

Mid term: When players of Visa’s scale continue to move in, it signals that stablecoin settlement is no longer a trial—it’s infrastructure. A combination of payment giants and exchanges will accelerate stablecoin adoption in real commercial settings. Regulators will also push countries to speed up stablecoin legislation. Binance Spot Trading Competition S3 Kicks Off: 500,000 USDC Prize Pool—Meet the Volume Requirement and You’re In

Binance’s spot trading tournament, Season 3, is here. The total prize pool is 500,000 USDC—more than double the 200,000 USDC tier commonly seen in the first two seasons. The rules are still the same “prize pool by trading volume ranking,” but this time there’s a more beginner-friendly twist: even if you don’t place in the top 1000, as long as your trading volume meets the requirement, you can still receive a proportional share from the 100,000 USDC contingency pool. In other words, this isn’t a pure “whale-only” grind—meet the threshold and you can still earn.

**I. How to Participate?**

1️⃣ Regular users and VIP users who complete identity verification can join (market makers and brokers are excluded). First, sign up on the event page.

2️⃣ During the event period, your cumulative spot trading volume must reach the equivalent of 500 USD—this is the entry threshold to be eligible for rewards. Note that volume from zero-fee trading pairs doesn’t count; both buy and sell orders are included.

3️⃣ The range of trading pairs is broad: 14 major pairs such as BTC/USDT, ETH/USDT, SOL/USDT, XRP/USDT, DOGE/USDT, ADA/USDT, SHIB/USDT, etc. all count—no need to trade small/meme coins.

4️⃣ There are two layers of sprint rewards: each of the two short periods (8/25–8/29 and 8/29–9/2) has its own ranking prizes. The top 5 get 5,000–15,000 USDC, and you can receive these along with the main prize pool at the same time—meaning the same trading volume can be counted twice.

**II. Time and Prize Pool Structure**

Main event period: August 25, 16:00 to September 8, 16:00 (Beijing time). The main prize pool of 400,000 USDC is distributed based on total trading volume rank: 1st place gets 15,000; top 5 are guaranteed at least 5,000; ranks 51–200 split 80,000 equally; ranks 201–1000 split 70,000 equally. All eligible participants outside the top 1000 share the remaining 100,000 USDC proportionally. Per-person maximum is 60 USDC. Rewards are issued as vouchers, distributed by September 22. Be sure to claim them in the Rewards Hub—expired vouchers are void.

**III. Who This Event Is For**

This is suitable for people who are already planning to trade on spot. The threshold is only 500 USD in trading volume, and all trading pairs are mainstream coins—basically turning your everyday trading activity into a voucher reward. What doesn’t work well is trying to boost volume just to chase rankings—your fee costs might exceed the contingency rewards, and the ranking portion is for the grinders/whales to compete.

The event may vary by region; eligibility and participation are subject to your account status and the official rules.

币安现货交易赛 S3 开跑：50 万 USDC 奖池，成交量达标就有份

币安现货交易锦标赛第三季来了，总奖池 50 万 USDC，比前两季常见的 20 万档直接翻了一倍多。规则还是那套"成交量排名分奖池"，但这次有个对普通人友好的设计：哪怕排不进前 1000 名，只要成交量达标，也能从 10 万 USDC 的兜底池里按比例分钱。也就是说这不是纯卷王游戏，达标就有得拿。

**一、怎么参加？**

1️⃣ 完成身份验证的普通用户和 VIP 用户都能玩（做市商和经纪商除外），先在活动页点报名。

2️⃣ 活动期内现货累计成交量达到 500 美元等值，这是拿奖的门槛线。注意零手续费交易对的量不算，买卖单都计入。

3️⃣ 交易对范围很宽：BTC/USDT、ETH/USDT、SOL/USDT、XRP/USDT、DOGE/USDT、ADA/USDT、SHIB/USDT 等 14 个主流对都算数,不需要去碰小币。

4️⃣ 冲刺奖励是第二层：8/25-8/29、8/29-9/2 两个短周期各设一份排名奖，前五名 5000-15000 USDC，可以和主奖池同时拿，相当于同一笔交易量被计算两次。

**二、时间和奖池结构**

主赛期：8 月 25 日 16:00 至 9 月 8 日 16:00（北京时间）。主奖池 40 万 USDC 按总成交量排名分：第 1 名 15000、前 5 名保底 5000，第 51-200 名均分 8 万，第 201-1000 名均分 7 万，1000 名之外的所有达标者按比例分剩余 10 万，单人上限 60 USDC。奖励是代金券形式，9 月 22 日前发放，记得去 Rewards Hub 领取，过期作废。

**三、这活动适合谁？**

适合本来就要在现货交易的人：门槛只有 500 美元成交量，交易对全是主流币，等于把日常交易顺手变现成一张代金券。不适合的是为了冲排名去放大交易量——手续费成本可能超过兜底奖励，排名部分让卷王们去争。活动可能因地区而异，以账户实际可参与状态和官方规则为准。

But if it breaks below 0.0162 with increased volume, then it means this pump was fake—admit you were wrong and get out directly. Don’t argue with money. For the mid-term, the key is whether it can hold 0.0168; if it can, there will likely be more to tell.

Next is PROM. I’m honestly a little tempted. The ZkEVM Layer 2 narrative is still riding the wave. Today it saw 2x volume, and the volume-price action is the healthiest among the three coins today. One last thing: in a broad “all-coin up” market, the scariest part isn’t missing the train—it’s chasing and getting trapped, then having your mindset blow up. Stick to your logic and your stop loss. ZKP这币……怎么说呢，涨幅27%放量2.6倍看着挺猛，但资金费率-0.0166%说明空头那边才是拥挤的一方，这种结构容易出反弹但持续性存疑。我自己的话，这个位置不会追，宁可等它回踩0.047-0.05区间再说。毕竟zkPass这个赛道我不算特别熟，看不懂的钱不赚，这是上次吃大亏学来的教训。

大盘情绪方面，恐惧贪婪指数50，标准的Neutral。这个位置我觉得挺舒服的——不是那种FOMO到极致的贪婪，也不是恐慌砸盘的恐惧。BTC在78K附近震荡，ETH在2.4K上方站稳，整体环境对山寨来说还算友好。但记住，这种行情最容易犯的错就是什么都想买，最后手里一堆没研究过的币。我今天就只看这Top3，其他的再涨也跟咱没关系。

最后说一句，这种普涨行情里，最怕的不是踏空，是追高被套然后心态爆炸。守住自己的逻辑和止损，剩下的交给市场。你们今天有吃到肉的吗？还是跟我一样只能看着别人吃？评论区聊聊呗。

Flowra opened an order-flow auction for Solana validators: the MEV “cake” will be sliced up again

Flowra launches an open order-flow auction, and the distribution landscape of Solana validators and MEV profits may be rewritten.

Flowra is bringing an open Orderflow Auction to Solana. In plain terms: previously, the order flow of users’ transactions on Solana was essentially monopolized by a few top-tier MEV infrastructure players, and validators had limited room to auction their right to order transactions within blocks. Now Flowra turns this auction into an open market—any validator can participate in bidding, making the value distribution of transaction flow more transparent. This is a bottom-layer plumbing-level change for the Solana ecosystem—not flashy, but it directly determines validators’ real earnings.

Market impact
- Short term: slightly neutral. Infrastructure news like this typically won’t directly move the SOL price. SOL is currently at $105.19, up 1.17% over the past 24h. It’s more like a broad market upswing, not closely related to this story.
- Medium term: mildly bullish. Higher actual validator earnings → staking yields become more attractive → positive for SOL’s staking demand. Meanwhile, an open auction compresses the profit margins of the top MEV oligarchs, sending more money back to validators and the wider ecosystem.

My take
I’m positive about this direction, but don’t expect it to act as a catalyst. With SOL hovering around $105, its short-term trend will still follow BTC’s rhythm ($78,105.38). The real point of interest is whether the order-flow auction can distribute Solana’s MEV annualized value (industry estimates: on the order of hundreds of millions to a few hundred million dollars) more fairly. If validator earnings genuinely improve, the SOL fundamental narrative will gain another piece. The risk is that during the initial rollout of the open auction, there could be technical glitches—similar mechanisms in the past have seen abnormal block production. Overall sentiment is bullish, but this is a slow-moving variable; don’t treat it as a reason for a short-term trade.

The Sandbox的跨链桥遭攻击，损失约70万美元。说实话这金额在币圈黑客事件里算小的，但项目方反应很快：直接宣布从项目国库拿出以太坊链上的SAND，对Base和BNB Chain上的合格持有人1:1赔付，赔付通道预计两周内开放。没有拖延、没有打折、没有甩锅给第三方，这在近年的桥被黑事件里算处理最利索的一档。

对市场的影响
- 短期：事件本身规模太小，对BTC $78,032、ETH $2,454这种主流盘基本没影响，SAND自身可能有情绪性波动但空间有限。真正值得注意的是，赔付用的SAND来自国库，等于增加潜在抛压。
- 中期：桥被黑后快速全额赔付，是行业危机公关的正面样本。过去两年桥被黑项目要么跑路要么打折赔，Sandbox这种做法如果成为标配，对小项目是压力，对行业信任是修复。

我的判断
中性偏谨慎。70万美元的案子不构成趋势性事件，SAND短线可能因赔付带来的国库释放承压，BTC、ETH继续按自己的宏观节奏走。风险点在于：两周赔付窗口前，攻击手法是否被复制到其他跨链桥上，那才是真正要盯的。

一句话翻译：钱不多，态度满分，但国库放币赔付对SAND持有者是隐性稀释。

Quantum computers haven’t arrived yet—Ripple first puts insurance on the XRP ledger: What exactly is Q-Day afraid of?

Ripple is rolling out a quantum-resistant upgrade for the XRP ledger in advance, to guard against the risk that future quantum computers may break current encryption algorithms.

Ripple has begun deploying preparations for post-quantum cryptography on the XRP Ledger (XRPL). The target is what the industry calls “Q-Day”—the day when quantum computers become powerful enough to crack existing elliptic-curve encryption. Once that day comes, private keys on-chain could potentially be reverse-engineered, directly exposing wallet addresses holding XRP. XRPL’s validating nodes and signature scheme need to migrate to post-quantum signature algorithms ahead of time. Put simply, it’s like changing door locks: it’s not that thieves have already entered—it’s that people know someday there will be tools that can open every lock, so they start swapping lock cores now.

One-sentence translation: Quantum threats are still a long-term risk, but blockchains must start changing the underlying encryption years in advance—and Ripple is acting early.

Impact on the market
- Short term: sentiment-led bullish for XRP. The post-quantum narrative adds a “long-term security” storyline point to XRP at $1.39, but note that the BTC $78,056.01 and ETH $2,455.23 charts are basically moving sideways, suggesting this kind of news doesn’t drive capital. Near-term volatility should be limited, and XRP will likely keep tracking the broader market.
- Medium term: post-quantum will gradually become a “baseline infrastructure compliance” requirement for public chains. If a chain delays upgrading, institutional money will likely penalize it. Ripple’s move may also pressure other chains to follow suit, and the “crypto security” narrative could be repeatedly traded.

My take
My view: neutral to bullish, but not a bullish catalyst you should realize immediately. Post-quantum is a slow-moving variable; what changes is the long-term valuation logic, not next week’s price. If XRP can hold above $1.39, it means the market is willing to price in the narrative. If it drops back quickly, then it’s just chasing the concept. The outlook is also positive for BTC and ETH over the long run—if the quantum threat is systematically solved by the industry, it removes the biggest tail risk hanging over crypto valuation. The risk is that if the post-quantum upgrade has technical vulnerabilities, it could trigger a second wave of panic. The main approach: stay cautious and watch how strongly the narrative gains traction.

The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) has publicly questioned the credibility of stablecoins being used for large-scale payments, and is pushing tokenized deposits.

What happened
The BIS chief went straight after it: stablecoins are not fit to handle large-scale payments. The reason is a lack of credibility—value is anchored on the issuer’s self-discipline, but the regulation and stability do not meet the standard. His proposed alternative is tokenized deposits—plainly, moving bank deposits on-chain. Issued by licensed banks, they are naturally regulated and backed by deposit insurance. BIS’s stance has been the same: financial innovation is fine, but control must remain within the banking system, and private stablecoins can’t be allowed to override monetary sovereignty.

The head of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) publicly questioned the payment capability of stablecoins, pushing tokenized bank deposits—directly targeting the very foundation that stablecoins rely on.

The BIS chief stated plainly: if stablecoins are used for large-scale payments, they lack credibility. His preferred alternative is tokenized deposits—tokenized deposits within the banking system—because stability and compliance are easier to control. In plain terms, traditional finance isn’t trying to reject on-chain—it's trying to make it happen on its own turf. The stablecoin market is currently over $200 billion. With USDT and USDC handling a large share of transaction settlement, the BIS’s message is essentially: your setup doesn’t work—you need to play by banking rules. He also mentioned that this involves global monetary sovereignty—if stablecoins grow large, central banks in many countries truly won’t be able to sleep.

Market impact
- Short term: a small negative sentiment shock. Stablecoins are core infrastructure in the crypto world. When a top authority points out “a lack of credibility,” funds will likely be more cautious in the short run. BTC is consolidating around $78,055, moving only 0.29% over 24h; ETH $2,456 is up slightly by 0.50%. The market already has no clear direction, so this kind of news is easy to be amplified in interpretation.
- Medium term: the regulatory trend is actually very clear—stablecoin legislation will accelerate, but compliance costs will rise, pushing smaller issuers out while benefiting the top players. In addition, the tokenized deposits narrative could be positive for RWA—banking tokenization is a trend, and BIS is simply making its stance explicit.

My take
View: This news is negative for the short term, but neutral to slightly positive for the medium term. BIS is criticizing unregulated stablecoins—not crypto itself. If banks actively move to tokenized deposits, it amounts to acknowledging that on-chain technology is the future. That logic doesn’t support a bearish stance on the crypto market. As long as BTC holds the $78,000 level, it remains a ranging market; only a breakdown would bring a new story. The key risk is that before the U.S. stablecoin bill is finalized, regulatory bluster may keep coming up—don’t let every single statement get you offside.

One-sentence translation: Traditional finance doesn’t want to block tokenization—it wants to grab the steering wheel.

- 短期：情绪面小利空。稳定币是币圈的基础设施，被权威机构点名“缺可信度”，资金短期会偏谨慎。BTC在$78,055附近横盘，24h只动0.29%，ETH $2,456微涨0.50%，市场本来就没什么方向，这种消息容易被放大解读。
- 中期：监管趋势其实很清晰了——稳定币立法会加速，但合规成本抬升，小发行方出局，头部受益。另外代币化存款这条线反而利好RWA叙事，银行上链是趋势，BIS只是把话挑明了。

我的判断
观点：这条消息短期利空、中期中性偏多。BIS骂的是无监管的稳定币，不是骂加密本身。银行主动搞代币化存款，等于承认链上技术是未来——这逻辑看空币圈说不通。BTC守住$78,000一线就还是震荡市，破位才有新故事。风险点在于美国稳定币法案落地前，监管嘴炮会反复出现，别被每句话都带节奏。
